$comment: The installer payload boundary (SCRUM-11123 Part C §10, Part M §28).
Default deny. A file produced by the Release publish reaches the MSI only when its relative
path matches an entry in 'allow'. Anything that matches nothing is dropped and reported, and
anything that matches 'denyAlways' fails the packaging build outright rather than being
quietly dropped — a test assembly, a customer database or a private key appearing in a
publish output is a defect in the publish, not something for the stager to tidy away.
Patterns are matched against the payload-relative path with forward slashes, case-insensitively,
$allowComment: '*.dll' is the self-contained .NET runtime and the WPF framework assemblies, which are the
point of the self-contained publish and cannot be enumerated by name across servicing
updates. '*/*.resources.dll' is the framework's and the product's satellite resources, one
culture folder deep. Neither widens the boundary to a second file type: no pattern here
matches .pdb, .cs, .csproj, .db, .zip, .png, .tif, .psd, .pfx or a folder more than one level
deep, so a payload can only ever be executable code, its two runtime .json descriptors and
$denyComment: Test assemblies, source, project files, any SQLite database, any signing or secret material,
customer and production imagery, the local override configuration, repository evidence and
any .git content. These are not expected in a Release publish of PrintFlow.App at all; the
list exists so that if one ever does appear the packaging build stops instead of shipping it.
'**/*.pdb' is a deliberate drop rather than an oversight: Release symbols are a release record,
not an installed file. Build-Installer.ps1 keeps them beside the .msi in the release folder and
the runbook says to archive them with the installer.
$requiredComment: The payload is incomplete without these, and a staging run that cannot produce every one of
